In a landscape where DIY electronics and open-source projects thrive, PCBWay has emerged as a vital player, offering enthusiasts the tools they need to bring their ideas to life. Colin recently shared his experience with PCBWay, detailing how the company has supported his BurgerDisk project by providing sponsorship for a full-size SD card module. 

Colin's journey with PCBWay began when he received an email from the company proposing to sponsor PCBs in exchange for a review. Having previously utilized their services for low-cost prototyping—five two-layer, non-assembled PCBs for just $12—Colin found himself drawn back to PCBWay despite an earlier switch to JLCPCB due to payment options. His return was fueled by the desire to create a robust SD card module, integral to his BurgerDisk project.

One of the standout features of PCBWay is its commitment to the open-source community. The company not only contributes significantly to projects like KiCad, donating at least $15,000 annually, but also provides a "Share & Sell" program that encourages users to share their open-source designs. This ethos resonates with Colin, who values the opportunity to engage with a platform that supports free software and collaboration among makers.

His previous experiences with JLCPCB, where design errors slipped through the cracks, highlighted the importance of careful checks. # Turn Your Best AI Prompts into One-Click Tools in Chrome

In an era where efficiency and productivity reign supreme, Google has unveiled a game-changing feature for Chrome users: the ability to transform your best AI prompts into one-click tools. This innovative functionality, aptly named "Skills," is set to revolutionize how we interact with AI, allowing for seamless integration of powerful capabilities directly into our browsing experience.

## Discovering and Saving Skills

The Skills feature allows users to discover, save, and customize AI workflows from their chat history. By simply typing a forward slash (/) or clicking a plus sign (+), users can access a library of ready-to-use Skills tailored for various tasks. This means that mundane processes—like calculating protein macros for recipes, generating product comparisons while shopping, or scanning documents for important information—can now be executed with a single click.

Imagine the convenience of having your most frequently used prompts at your fingertips, eliminating the need to retype or search through chat histories. One user even mentioned their go-to prompt that encourages concise, machine-like responses: "No emojis. Be concise. No suggestions unless I explicitly ask for them." This highlights the diverse ways individuals can tailor their Skills for personal or professional use.

## A Library of Ready-to-Use Skills

The Skills library is designed to cater to common tasks, empowering users to customize as needed. Health enthusiasts can quickly assess nutritional information, while busy professionals can streamline their workflow with AI-powered document analysis. The potential applications are vast, inviting users to explore creative uses of AI in their daily lives.

However, as with any technological advancement, concerns about security and privacy arise. Google assures users that Skills are built on Chrome’s robust security foundation, requiring confirmation for sensitive actions like adding calendar events or sending emails. This commitment to safety aims to mitigate fears surrounding the introduction of such powerful tools.

## The Conversation Around Skills

The announcement of Skills has sparked lively discussions among tech enthusiasts. Many users expressed excitement about the potential for automation. One comment noted, "This could be interesting," reflecting the general intrigue surrounding the feature. Others shared their personal use cases, emphasizing how Skills could enhance productivity, particularly in managing repetitive tasks.

Yet, the conversation also took a critical turn. Some commenters raised questions about the reliability of AI responses, pointing out the inconsistency often experienced with AI models. This tension between enthusiasm for innovation and skepticism about execution is common in discussions about emerging technologies.

## Enabling the Future of Automation

For those eager to try out this feature, it's currently rolling out in Gemini on Chrome for users with English-US settings on Mac, Windows, and ChromeOS. To activate Skills, users can enable it through Chrome flags and start exploring the browsing experience enhanced by AI.

# Exploring Plain: A Python Framework Designed for Humans and Agents

In the ever-evolving landscape of web development, frameworks come and go, but one recent entrant is creating buzz within the tech community. Enter **Plain**, a Python web framework that positions itself as a solution for both human developers and artificial agents. With a growing repository on GitHub, Plain boasts an impressive 783 stars and over 36,000 commits, signaling a robust and engaged development community.

## A Fresh Take on Web Development

At its core, Plain aims to simplify the web development process by offering a familiar yet reimagined foundation. The framework emphasizes a clear, typed, and predictable code structure, making it easier for developers—whether human or agent—to understand and utilize. Its class-based views and router class for URL handling are designed to streamline the development process, while built-in tooling for agents ensures that common mistakes are mitigated effectively.

### Getting Started with Plain

For those eager to dive in, getting started with Plain is straightforward. A simple command creates a new app:

```bash
mkdir my-app && cd my-app && claude "$(curl -sSf https://plainframework.com/start.md)"
```

This command sets the stage for developers to build applications quickly and efficiently. Plain's command-line interface includes essential commands such as `plain dev` for starting a development server, `plain fix` for linting and formatting code, and `plain test` for running tests with pytest.

## The Agent Factor

The intriguing aspect of Plain is its focus on "agents." In recent discussions within the tech community, the idea of creating tools specifically for artificial intelligence agents has sparked debate. Some argue that developing frameworks tailored to agents may be counterproductive, as these entities are already proficient in using established technologies like Python and Django.

However, proponents of Plain suggest that the framework's opinionated defaults and structured documentation can significantly reduce the cognitive load for agents. By minimizing the surface area over which agents must reason, Plain may offer a more efficient pathway for AI to assist in coding tasks.

### Community Reactions: A Mixed Bag

As with any new technology, reactions to Plain have been varied. Some users express excitement about the potential of an agent-optimized framework, highlighting the need for tools that simplify complexity in coding. Others remain skeptical, questioning whether a new framework is genuinely necessary or if existing solutions suffice.

In a lively Hacker News thread, one commenter noted that agents can learn new specifications effectively, which challenges the notion that they should only use established tools. Another perspective shared in the discussion emphasized the importance of predictability and consistency in interfaces, arguing that agents are adept at learning from well-structured documentation.

Conversely, critics point out that the framework may not significantly outperform existing options. Some users even speculated that Plain might be an arbitrary fork of Django with minimal enhancements, while others celebrated it as a necessary evolution in the face of growing AI integration.

# Transforming Idle Hardware into AI Supercomputers: Exploring AgentFM

In the ever-evolving landscape of artificial intelligence, innovative solutions often emerge from the most unexpected sources. Enter AgentFM, a groundbreaking project that promises to turn idle hardware into a decentralized AI supercomputer. This initiative not only taps into underutilized resources but also fosters a collaborative environment for AI development.

## What is AgentFM?

AgentFM is designed to harness the power of idle GPUs, transforming them into a peer-to-peer (P2P) networking grid that can run advanced AI algorithms. This concept is reminiscent of initiatives like SETI@home, which allowed ordinary users to contribute their computational power to scientific research. However, AgentFM pivots this model towards artificial intelligence, enabling a community-driven approach to building and refining AI agents.

### Core Features

The project boasts a range of impressive features that set it apart:

- **Zero-Config P2P Networking**: Users can connect their hardware effortlessly, eliminating complex setup processes.
- **Ephemeral Sandboxing & Artifact Routing**: This ensures that AI workloads are secure and efficiently managed.
- **GossipSub Load Balancing**: This feature optimizes the distribution of tasks across the network, improving performance.
- **Framework & Language Agnostic**: AgentFM supports various programming languages and frameworks, making it accessible to a wider audience.
- **Command Center**: The integrated Radar UI and API Gateway provide users with a comprehensive management interface.

### Installation Made Easy

Getting started with AgentFM is straightforward. Users can install the necessary components with a simple command:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://api.agentfm.net/install.sh | bash
```

From cloning the repository to running local large language models (LLMs), the steps are clearly outlined, ensuring that even those with minimal technical expertise can dive into the world of AI development.

### Why It Matters

As the demand for AI capabilities increases, so does the necessity for efficient resource utilization. Many GPUs remain underutilized in personal computers, and AgentFM addresses this by enabling users to contribute their spare computing power to a collective AI effort. This not only democratizes access to AI but also promotes community engagement and innovation.

### Community Conversations

The announcement of AgentFM has sparked conversations among tech enthusiasts, with comments highlighting its potential. One user likened it to "SETI@home... but for AI agents," reflecting the excitement around this novel approach to computational resource sharing. Such enthusiasm is indicative of a growing interest in collaborative AI projects that leverage decentralized technologies.

## Conclusion

AgentFM represents a significant step forward in the realm of decentralized AI computing. By turning idle hardware into a robust network of AI agents, it not only enhances computational capabilities but also fosters a community-oriented approach to technological advancement. As we continue to explore the possibilities of artificial intelligence, initiatives like AgentFM remind us that innovation often lies in our willingness to collaborate and share resources.
